segments.speaker: COUNSELLOR
segments.en: Hi there, Kate. Come on in. How are you today?

segments.speaker: KATE
segments.en: Fine thanks.

segments.speaker: COUNSELLOR
segments.en: Hi, Luki. How's things?

segments.speaker: LUKI
segments.en: OK.

segments.speaker: COUNSELLOR
segments.en: Well, as I explained on the phone, I'm a counsellor here at the Student Services section of the university and I'm interviewing overseas students to help me draw up a guide for new students so I'd be grateful if you could tell me a little about your time since you've been here in Cambridge.

segments.speaker: KATE
segments.en: Right.

segments.speaker: LUKI
segments.en: Good idea.

segments.speaker: COUNSELLOR
segments.en: Now, Kate let's start with you. OK, um, this is your second semester isn't it? Could you tell us something about your first impressions of the town when you arrived?

segments.speaker: KATE
segments.en: Yeah well first of all I was struck by how quiet it is here in the evening

segments.speaker: COUNSELLOR
segments.en: Yes, I suppose Cambridge is a quiet place. Where did you live when you first arrived?

segments.speaker: KATE
segments.en: Well, I went straight into student accommodation; it was a kind of student hostel.

segments.speaker: COUNSELLOR
segments.en: Ah right, so you didn't have to worry about doing your own cooking or anything like that?

segments.speaker: KATE
segments.en: No, but sometimes I wished I had! The food at the hostel was awful.

segments.speaker: COUNSELLOR
segments.en: Oh dear. But how were the other students?

segments.speaker: KATE
segments.en: To be honest I haven’t managed to make many friends even though the place is full. People seem to keep to themselves; they’re not really very friendly.

segments.speaker: COUNSELLOR
segments.en: Oh I’m sorry to hear that. Well, what about the actual course? You’re studying … uh?

segments.speaker: KATE
segments.en: I’m doing a Masters by coursework in Environmental Studies.

segments.speaker: COUNSELLOR
segments.en: Ah, right, and how are you finding that?

segments.speaker: KATE
segments.en: Yeah, well, it’s been pretty good really. I’ve enjoyed the course, but I feel there hasn’t been enough contact with the lecturers. They all seem to be incredibly busy. The only chance I’ve really had to talk to them was on the field trip.

segments.speaker: COUNSELLOR
segments.en: Well that’s no good. Could anything be done to improve the course in your opinion?

segments.speaker: KATE
segments.en: Well … I think it would be helpful to have meetings with lecturers on the course. Say once a fortnight — something like that.

segments.speaker: COUNSELLOR
segments.en: Regular meetings. Yes that could certainly help. Now Kate, we’ll come back to you in a minute, but I’d just like to ask Luki some questions.

segments.speaker: COUNSELLOR
segments.en: Luki, where are you from?

segments.speaker: LUKI
segments.en: I am from Indonesia.

segments.speaker: COUNSELLOR
segments.en: And how did you find Cambridge when you first arrived?

segments.speaker: LUKI
segments.en: Well, I like it here. I think the city is very beautiful.

segments.speaker: COUNSELLOR
segments.en: What about your accommodation? Was that OK?

segments.speaker: LUKI
segments.en: Yes, OK. At first I stayed with a family for three months. They were very kind to me but they had three young children and I found it difficult to study

segments.speaker: COUNSELLOR
segments.en: Right, I see.

segments.speaker: LUKI
segments.en: So after three months I moved out and now I live with two other students in a student house. It’s much cheaper and we like it there.

segments.speaker: COUNSELLOR
segments.en: Good, and what about your studies? What are you studying?

segments.speaker: LUKI
segments.en: I’m doing a Bachelor of Computing.

segments.speaker: COUNSELLOR
segments.en: Computing. I see. Um, apart from the language difficulties, if you can separate them, how have you found the course?

segments.speaker: LUKI
segments.en: OK, but …

segments.speaker: COUNSELLOR
segments.en: Yes, go on.

segments.speaker: LUKI
segments.en: Well, the main difficulty for me is getting time on the computers in the computer room. It’s always busy and this makes it very hard to do my practical work.

segments.speaker: COUNSELLOR
segments.en: Yes, I’m sure it would. Can you reserve time in the computer room?

segments.speaker: LUKI
segments.en: No, you can’t … but it would certainly help if we could reserve computer time.

segments.speaker: COUNSELLOR
segments.en: Yes. I’ll look into that and see if something can’t be done to improve things over there. Now let’s go back to Kate...
